REASONING: The 1.1 run confirms the mixture story and suggests a rising bad-state probability above T=1.0: about 2.2% at 1.0, 17.5% at 1.1, 20% at 1.2. Good-state mean declines with T above 1.0; bad-state mean is fairly stable around 88. We now have enough to draft a generative model: sample a latent bad/good indicator with p_bad(T) given by a clipped quadratic fit to observed rates, then draw from a Normal whose mean is a quadratic (good) or near-constant/slight linear (bad), with fixed SD by state. Before submitting, I want to compute these fits numerically from the data so the code can use concrete coefficients.
```python
import numpy as np, pandas as pd

# collect experimental lots only (controlled T points) plus archive at 1.0 for mixture estimate
frames = []
for name in ["df", "df_exp", "exp11"]:
    if name in globals():
        tmp = globals()[name].copy()
        if "lot_id" in tmp.columns:
            frames.append(tmp[["lot_id","T","y"]])
dat = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True).drop_duplicates()

threshold = 89.0
dat["bad"] = (dat["y"] < threshold).astype(float)

# fit bad probability quadratic in T
p_by_T = dat.groupby("T")["bad"].agg(["mean","count","sum"]).reset_index()
coef_p = np.polyfit(p_by_T["T"], p_by_T["mean"], 2)

# conditional fits
good = dat[dat["bad"] == 0]
bad = dat[dat["bad"] == 1]

coef_good = np.polyfit(good["T"], good["y"], 2)
coef_bad = np.polyfit(bad["T"], bad["y"], 1)

sd_good = good["y"].std(ddof=1)
sd_bad = bad["y"].std(ddof=1)

print("p_by_T:")
print(p_by_T)
print("\ncoef_p quadratic:", coef_p)
print("coef_good quadratic:", coef_good)
print("coef_bad linear:", coef_bad)
print("sd_good:", sd_good)
print("sd_bad:", sd_bad)

# sanity-check predicted values on grid
grid = np.array([0.6,0.8,1.0,1.1,1.2,1.4])
pred = pd.DataFrame({
    "T": grid,
    "p_bad_raw": np.polyval(coef_p, grid),
    "mu_good": np.polyval(coef_good, grid),
    "mu_bad": np.polyval(coef_bad, grid),
})
pred["p_bad_clipped"] = pred["p_bad_raw"].clip(0.001, 0.35)
print("\npredictions:")
print(pred)
```
